title: Count the Results, Then the Robots

lanes_searched: Humanoid and general-purpose robots doing real work in factories or warehouses
Industrial robot arms, collaborative robots and automation vendors
Mining, construction, ports, agriculture and energy automation
AI models and software for robots aimed at industrial tasks
Deployments and rollouts announced by companies that use the technology
Funding rounds, acquisitions, partnerships and joint ventures
Robot hardware, components and supply chain
Safety standards, certification, regulation and government programmes
Research papers and open-source releases with near-term industrial relevance

kept.title: ASICS discloses faster inventory recovery with autonomous warehouse drones
kept.reason: ASICS provides the week's most useful buying evidence by showing how inventory automation affects recovery time and counting workload, while leaving costs and payback open.

kept.title: Path Robotics raises $300 million to expand adaptive welding into broader manufacturing
kept.reason: The $300 million financing is a substantial bet on automating variable fabrication work, although the claimed customer economics remain unverified.

kept.title: GXO and Apptronik outline conditional deployment of up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids
kept.reason: GXO's conditional framework gives logistics buyers a concrete procurement development to watch, provided the proposed 1,000 robots are not presented as firm orders.

kept.title: Beijing adopts robot-industry plan linking industrial applications, manufacturing and safety assurance
kept.reason: Beijing's adopted plan could shape a major robotics supplier cluster through coordinated applications, manufacturing and assurance work, though its targets are not funded delivery commitments.

kept.title: Runway releases Praxis-1 robot-model weights and commercial-use code
kept.reason: Downloadable weights and commercial-use permission materially change access and supplier options for automation teams, without establishing production readiness.

cut.title: Google reports 96% automotive-kitting success with Gemini Robotics 2.5 at Mercedes-Benz
cut.reason: The vendor-reported kitting result lacks enough trial detail to change a buying decision and overlaps with the stronger customer-confirmed Apptronik story.

cut.title: Agile Robots raises $500 million for US expansion and manufacturing capacity
cut.reason: Path wins the single funding slot with a clearer industrial application, while Agile's broad expansion plans lack investment allocations or construction schedules.

cut.title: NTT reports fewer loading failures using a physics-informed world model
cut.reason: The controlled loading experiment offers less immediate decision value than this week's customer evidence and capital commitments, with airport implementation still unspecified.
